content.title: About
content.content: Pork is the meat of domestic pigs, and a pork steak (NS) refers to a cut that is grilled or pan‑seared. It has a mild flavor, moderate fat content, and the characteristic aroma of pork. The steak is usually served as a main dish and can be paired with a variety of sauces and sides.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
NS pork steak is often cut from the loin or shoulder, giving it a tender texture.
Different cultures feature pork in traditional dishes ranging from barbecue to roasts.
Pork provides all essential amino acids needed by humans.
When cooked properly, the steak retains most of its nutrients.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork steak supplies high‑quality protein that supports muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains B1, B3, B6 and B12, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is essential for immune function, wound healing, and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: The iron in pork is highly bioavailable and helps prevent anemia.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: In moderate amounts, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats in pork support heart health.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked pork can harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or Trichinella.

items.title: Allergy and sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may react to pork proteins.

items.title: Sodium in processed versions
items.content: Marinated or smoked steaks can be high in salt, which is undesirable for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pork steak to medium doneness, slice against the grain, and serve with vegetables, potatoes or whole‑grain sides. Complement with yogurt‑based, mustard or tomato sauces for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak refrigerated at 0–4 °C for no more than 2–3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for 4–6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
